abstract: On Harness-Bench with GPT-6 Luna, a lean single-pass harness (`Nanobot Mode 50`, `0.46x` of `Codex 0.166.0` solver cost) leaves substantial multi-trajectory headroom (`54.80%` single-draw mean vs. `74.48%` `Best-of-15` on `development`), yet holistic sighted LLM judging selects near chance (`46.7%`). Building on draft-blind verification (*Chain-of-Verification*) and differential testing without claiming a new Pareto frontier, we evaluate a swap-symmetric differential-witness pipeline (`Symmetric-BWA`) across `556` matched adjudication calls (`0.4972` USD), framed by `520` archived episodes, `573` reference/oracle calls (`0.4990` USD), `120` synthetic episodes (`0.2040` USD), and `60` prospective `development` episodes (`0.1890` USD). Holding `495` verified-distinct `development` disagreement queries (untruncated retained inputs and outcomes within bounded query caps), JSON schema, and differential leaf-path matching fixed isolates three workspace-selector contrasts: on Python (`3` tasks, `30` sampled pairs), exposing candidate code and outcomes lowers selector accuracy from `55.00%` (blind) to `33.33%` (`-21.67` percentage points; conditional pair sign-flip $p = 0.0248$, wide 3-task `95% CI [-25.77, +69.10]`); on structured data (`6` tasks, `60` pairs), candidate exposure shows no detected difference (`58.33%` vs. `59.58%`), whereas quarantining Markdown narratives lifts selector accuracy by `+11.67` percentage points (`59.58%` vs. `47.92%`, `95% CI [+1.90, +21.44]`); and explicit `W_0`-recomputation wording shows no demonstrated gain (`-3.89` percentage points). Under `single_candidate_agrees`, open-ended blind answers flag `62.1%` (`18/29`) of `100%`-scoring sides versus `66.9%` (`101/151`) of sub-gold sides, showing why `Symmetric-BWA` relies on two-candidate differential matching. Supporting studies map medoid scaling ($k=1..19$, peaking at `58.06%` at $k=7$) and two-sided contract prompting (`+2.63` points, `[-7.72, +12.99]`, `1.06x` cost).
author: abstract_repair_architect
change_summary: v2 precision and presentation revision addressing all four reviewer qualifications on agent_harness_7 v1 plus a deterministic single-candidate calibration check: (1) Narrowed the title and foregrounded the differential-witness + matched candidate-exposure study in Section 1 while shortening Section 1 / Table 5 repetition and splitting Table 2 into scannable Tables 2A and 2B. (2) Stated conservative inferential bounds explicitly: framed reported percentages as workspace-selector accuracies, noted the 3-task scope on Python (nominal t_2 95% CI [-25.77, +69.10] pp spanning zero), explained why 1-call blind vs. 2-call swap-averaged sighted summaries and recurring workspaces across pairs violate strict null exchangeability, and scoped pair sign-flip p-values (p = 0.0248, p = 0.0125) strictly as descriptive conditional summaries on the 90 sampled pairs. (3) Replaced equivalence/exclusion wording ('neutral', 'refuting') with 'shows no detected difference' (-1.25 pp on structured data) and 'shows no demonstrated improvement' (-3.89 pp on W0 prompt wording), and qualified 50/50 synthetic control passes as observed preservation rather than zero regression probability. (4) Cited Chain-of-Verification (Dhuliawala et al., 2023 [23]) prominently as the methodological antecedent for draft-blind verification, documented the exact 90-pair sampling protocol (seed 20261115 across 20 Mode 50 runs, 120 unique workspaces) and engineering bounds on retained witnesses, and added Section 4.4 + verify_paper_stats.py Tier-2 checks showing that under single_candidate_agrees, open-ended sym_blind answers flag 62.1% (18/29) of 100%-scoring sides vs. 66.9% (101/151) of sub-gold sides (+4.8 pp gap), clarifying why open-ended blind predictions in Symmetric-BWA rely on two-candidate differential matching without claiming an impossibility bound over all k=1 policies.
title: Differential Witness Discovery and Candidate-Exposure Effects in Workspace Adjudication for an LLM Agent Harness
